Services Analyzer — Manual

A single-file, no-install Windows tool for services triage: every service and driver the SYSTEM hive configures, joined to its install history from the System and Security event logs, and scored for persistence and remote-execution tradecraft. Part of the DFIR-Windows-Artifact-Finder toolkit; runs Eric Zimmerman's RECmd and EvtxECmd for you.

Author: Ben Morris github.com/bpmorris22/Services-Analyzer MIT licence App v0.1.2 Manual updated 2026-10-03 All screenshots use synthetic data (host WKS-0142, domain CONTOSO)

1  What it answers

What is configured to run? — every service and driver: binary, ServiceDLL, run-as account, start mode, recovery command, key LastWrite.
What was installed, when, and by whom? — 7045 / 4697 install events, 7040 start-type changes, crashes and start failures.
What was installed and is no longer there? — the join: an install with no matching service key is a transient or deleted service.

That third question is the reason the tool exists. Remote-execution tools — PsExec, Impacket's smbexec / psexec, sc create one-shots — create a service, run it once and delete it. The SYSTEM hive no longer holds it, so a registry-only view never sees it; an event-log-only view sees the install but not what is configured beside it. Services Analyzer reads both and lines them up, so a deleted service sits in the same table as the configured ones, tagged LOG-ONLY.

2  Requirements & setup

  • Windows with the built-in mshta.exe — double-click Services-Analyzer.hta. No install, no admin (except where the evidence itself needs it).
  • RECmd (required for the hive) — the whole RECmd folder, because the Services plugin lives in Plugins\RegistryPlugin.Services.dll. Put it next to the .hta (<app>\RECmd\) or keep it in C:\ZimmermanTools; Update / download RECmd fetches the official zip.
  • EvtxECmd (optional, for the logs) — the whole folder incl. Maps\, same places; Update / download EvtxECmd fetches it. Without it, runs are hive-only.
  • .NET runtime matching the EZ build you use — runs set DOTNET_ROLL_FORWARD=Major so newer runtimes work.
  • When the engines are not next to the app, a launch without arguments offers to download them there (the toolkit is meant to be self-contained); Cancel keeps using the copy it found.

3  Quick start

  1. Folder… → pick a host's collection folder (a Velociraptor Collection-<host>-<time> folder, a KAPE target folder, or any folder holding config\SYSTEM and winevt\Logs\). The app searches it and fills the three source boxes. A single SYSTEM hive or .evtx works too (File…).
  2. Check the Target hostname guess (from the Collection-<host>-… segment) — it names the output folder.
  3. Process → analyze. A console shows [1/3] RECmd … [3/3] EvtxECmd; the app stays responsive and loads the results when done. A typical host takes under a minute — Security.evtx is the slow one.
Control panel after Folder… on a synthetic collection: SYSTEM hive, System.evtx and Security.evtx located, hostname guessed (WKS-0142), output folder derived, toolkit IOC.txt merged.
If the folder holds several SYSTEM hives (several collections of one host, or a multi-host root), a chooser appears — one host per run, newest collection first. Logs are paired to the chosen hive inside the same collection, never across hosts.

4  The three sources

SourceEngineWhat it adds
SYSTEM hive (config\SYSTEM)RECmd, an embedded batch (ServicesAnalyzer.reb) — the Services plugin plus ObjectName, FailureCommand, ServiceMain, the current control set and ComputerNameWhat is configured: name, display name, start mode, type, binary, ServiceDLL, run-as account, recovery command, key LastWrite. Every control set is read; the current one is listed, services found only in another set are kept (OLDSET).
System.evtxEvtxECmd --inc 7045,7040,7034,7031,7030,7023,7024,7000,7009Installs (7045, with the installer's SID), start-type changes (7040), crashes (7031 / 7034) and start failures (7000 / 7009 / 7023 / 7024 / 7030). Its time span is the "log coverage" used by NO7045.
Security.evtxEvtxECmd --inc 46974697 installs, which name the installing account and logon ID. Present only where "Security System Extension" auditing is on — and when present, they also turn bare 7045 SIDs into names.
  • Hive-only run (no logs, or no EvtxECmd): every hive rule works; there is no install history, so LOG-ONLY and USER-INSTALL cannot fire.
  • Events-only run (logs, no hive): every install becomes a log-only record by definition, so LOG-ONLY is not scored; the image / account / name rules still apply.
  • Dirty hives: RECmd replays .LOG1/.LOG2 beside the hive. A dirty hive without its logs makes RECmd abort — the app retries that step once with --nl and says so in the status.

5  Reading the results

Overview

The stat row reflects the active filters: services, Win32 vs drivers, autostart, installs logged, log-only, suspicious, IOC hits, which sources were loaded, the System log's coverage and the hive's own ComputerName. Below it: installs by service, the newest lone key writes (bulk servicing rewrites excluded), and the suspicious services by score. Every name is clickable — it becomes the search filter.

Overview of the synthetic host: 86 services, 6 suspicious. The suspicious list already tells the story — a random-named log-only service, a fake updater in ProgramData, a driver dropped in Windows\Temp, a svchost DLL in a user folder, PsExec, and Defender turned off.

Services view

One row per service: the current control set, plus services only in another set, plus services seen only in the logs. Default sort is score, descending; suspicious rows (score ≥ 3) are shaded. Columns: Tags · Name · Display name · Start · Type · Account · Binary (resolved, arguments greyed) · ServiceDLL · Key LastWrite · Installed (first install, ×count) · Installed by · Source.

  • Chips with live counts: tags (Suspicious, IOC, Remote exec, LOLBin, User path, User install, Defense off), type (Win32 / Drivers), start (Autostart = Boot + System + Automatic, Manual, Disabled), source (Hive / Hive+Log / Log-only).
  • Source: HIVE = configured, no install in the loaded logs · HIVE+LOG = configured and its install was logged · LOG-ONLY = installed per the logs, no service key left.
  • account: dropdown, or click any Account cell, to filter by run-as account (drivers and services with no ObjectName group as (drivers / no account)).
  • Search, the activity-date window (a service passes when its key write, an install or a start-type change falls inside), IOC / keywords, Export view → CSV, Copy for case notes. Columns are resizable and remembered.
Services view, score-ranked. Hover a tag for the reasons; dashed BULK tags mark key writes that were part of a servicing burst (context only — never scored).

Timeline

Everything with a time on one stream, newest first: installs (Install 7045, Install 4697, or Install 7045+4697 when both logged the same install), start-type changes collapsed per service per day (×N), crashes and start failures, lone service-key writes, and one row per bulk rewrite ("74 service keys rewritten within 1 s — servicing / bulk update, not install times"). Rows inherit their service's tags and shading.

Timeline: the 2026-09-27 01:58–02:31 burst — PsExec, a vulnerable driver, Defender disabled, an smbexec-style install that fails to start, a fake updater, then a svchost DLL service written straight into the registry (a key write with no install event).

Accounts

Services grouped by run-as account: count, autostart, drivers, suspicious, max score, newest key write. A real account (CONTOSO\svc_backup) running a service is worth a look on its own; click a group to filter the Services view to it.

Accounts view. Built-in identities (LocalSystem, LocalService, NetworkService) carry nearly everything; the one domain account stands out.

Detail pane

Click any row. You get every scoring reason with its points, every field (raw ImagePath, resolved binary, arguments, ServiceDLL — split when RECmd reports it at both levels — ServiceMain, FailureCommand, group, privileges, both LastWrites), the other control set's values when they differ, the full install history (time, which events, the name as logged, image, start, account, installer, and what the join matched on), start-type changes and crashes / failures. copy record puts a case-notes block on the clipboard.

Detail of the smbexec-style service: cmd.exe running an echo-redirect-delete chain to a loopback admin share, installed by CONTOSO\jdoe-adm, failing to start 30 s later (7009 / 7000) — and absent from the hive.

6  How the join works

7045 logs the service's display name when one was supplied, not its key name, so a name-only match misses most vendor services. Each install is matched to a hive service in this order — the first hit wins:

  1. the event's name equals a service key name;
  2. the event's name equals a service display name (resource-string display names like @%SystemRoot%\…,-2 can't be resolved offline and are skipped);
  3. the key name in parentheses at the end of the event's name (Microsoft Edge Update Service (edgeupdate));
  4. the key name from the paired 4697 (below);
  5. a unique image path — only when exactly one hive service uses that command line.

7045 ↔ 4697 pairing. When auditing is on, one install is logged twice. A 7045 and a 4697 within ±2 s are paired on name evidence first (same name, the 4697 key's display name equals the 7045 name, or the key in parentheses). A shared image alone pairs them only when it is unambiguous both ways — two services installed together from one binary are left unpaired rather than crossed.

Installs with no match become LOG-ONLY records named after the key (from 4697) or the logged name. A record shows its newest install's configuration; every image it ever had is scored. Start-type changes attach by key name (7040 carries it), and crashes / failures by the key name SCM writes into the event's binary data.

7  Scoring reference

Rules add points; a service with score ≥ 3 is suspicious. Hover a tag in the app for the exact reason. The case window never changes a score.

TagPtsFires when
IOC+3An IOC / keyword (incl. the toolkit IOC.txt) is in the name, display name, any image, ServiceDLL, failure command or account.
USERPATH+3The binary or ServiceDLL sits in a user-writable folder: \Users\, \AppData\, \Temp\ (incl. Windows\Temp), \Users\Public\, \Downloads\, \PerfLogs\, $Recycle.Bin, non-Microsoft \ProgramData\. The binary only — never its arguments.
LOLBIN+3The binary is an interpreter / LOLBin: cmd, powershell, pwsh, mshta, wscript, cscript, regsvr32, rundll32, msiexec, certutil, bitsadmin, java(w), node, python. svchost and the Windows Installer service (msiexec /V) are exempt.
REMOTE-EXEC+3The command line carries remote-execution tradecraft: \\127.0.0.1\, \\localhost\, \\%COMPUTERNAME%\, ADMIN$, C$\__, cmd /Q /c, an echo … > … & … & del chain, encoded PowerShell.
TOOLNAME+2Service name is a remote-exec tool default: PSEXESVC, PAExec*, RemCom*, csexec*, winexesvc, BTOBTO (dual-use — a review flag, not a verdict).
SVCDLL+2A ServiceDLL outside system32, Program Files, DriverStore or the Defender platform folder.
DRVPATH+2A driver whose image is outside system32\drivers, DriverStore, Program Files or the Defender platform folder (bring-your-own-vulnerable-driver staging).
DEFENSE-OFF+2Defender, its network inspection service, Sense, Security Center, Windows Security, the firewall, Event Log or Sysmon is Disabled in the hive, or a 7040 switched it to disabled. Legitimate for Defender beside a third-party AV.
USER-INSTALL+2Installed by a user account — a 7045 SID that isn't SYSTEM / LocalService / NetworkService, or a 4697 subject that isn't SYSTEM or a machine account (…$).
FAILCMD+1A FailureCommand (recovery program) is set; its own binary is checked by USERPATH / LOLBIN / REMOTE-EXEC too (vendor cmd /c <Windows or Program Files>\…\x.bat recovery scripts are exempt from LOLBIN).
ACCOUNT+1Runs as a real account rather than LocalSystem, NT AUTHORITY\*, NT SERVICE\* or a driver object.
RANDNAME+1Random-looking name (Impacket / Metasploit style). Tuned to zero false positives on ~930 real service names; catches only part of truly random names — a hint.
OLDSET+1Only present in a non-current control set (removed from the live configuration).
LOG-ONLY+1Installed per the logs, no matching service key — transient or deleted. Low on purpose: vendor updaters do this too. Not scored in events-only runs.
NO7045+1A Win32 service key written (outside a bulk rewrite) inside the System log's coverage with no install event and no 7040 to explain it — created by a direct registry write, or the log was cleared.
NOSVC+1A 7000 / 7009 start failure within 60 s of the install — the "binary" was a command, not a real service.
RECENT+1A lone key write within 30 days of the hive's newest service-key write (the hive's own clock, never the case window). Not added on top of NO7045.
AUTOSTART+1Boot / System / Automatic start and one of USERPATH, LOLBIN, REMOTE-EXEC, SVCDLL, DRVPATH.

Context tags, no points: BULK — the key's LastWrite is inside a mass rewrite (≥ 10 service keys within ±2 s: Windows servicing or an installer). Key LastWrite is not install time; BULK keys never count as recent. CSDIFF — another control set holds a different image, ServiceDLL or start mode (see the detail pane).

Calibration: on two real hosts (a workstation with ~850 services and a server with ~600) the tuned rules flagged 2 and 0 services — the workstation's two being a genuine smbexec service and a kernel driver loaded from Windows\Temp. Expect single digits on a clean host; read each one.

8  Worked example — a lateral-movement night

The screenshots use a synthetic host, WKS-0142, with one planted intrusion by CONTOSO\jdoe-adm on 2026-09-27. Read it the way you would a real case — Timeline first, then the detail panes:

UTCWhat the tool showsWhy it matters
01:58:30PSEXESVC — Install 7045+4697, LOG-ONLY, TOOLNAME USER-INSTALLPsExec came in with a domain admin account and cleaned up after itself.
02:05:40RTCore64 kernel driver from C:\Windows\Temp — USERPATH DRVPATH USER-INSTALLA vulnerable signed driver staged for defence evasion.
02:08:12WinDefend start type → disabled (7040), Disabled in the hive — DEFENSE-OFFDefender switched off minutes after the driver landed.
02:14:09xVRKqLmB — cmd.exe echo / redirect / delete via \\127.0.0.1\C$\__output, fails to start 30 s later — LOG-ONLY, score 11Impacket smbexec: the service is the command, so SCM reports a start failure every time.
02:20:51WinUpdHelper "Windows Update Helper" from C:\ProgramData\WinUpd\updsvc_x64.exe, Automatic — IOC USERPATH USER-INSTALLPersistence dressed as a Windows component; the toolkit IOC list already knows the binary name.
02:31:02NetSvcHost svchost service with ServiceDLL C:\Users\Public\Libraries\nethost.dll — key write, no install event — NO7045Created by writing the registry directly, so no 7045 exists — only the hive shows it.

The noise around it — 74 service keys rewritten in one second on 2026-09-10 (servicing), 42 BITS start-type flaps, Edge Update installed by the machine account, two Print Spooler crashes, a backup agent running as CONTOSO\svc_backup — stays unflagged or at 1–2 points.

9  Command line & the Artifact Finder

mshta "Services-Analyzer.hta" "<input>" ["<outDir>"] [/auto] [/from:yyyy-MM-dd] [/to:yyyy-MM-dd]
  • <input> — a collection / host folder, a SYSTEM hive or an .evtx (sources located; processed with /auto), a .csv this app produced (the whole run reloads), or an output folder holding its runinfo.json (newest run reloads).
  • <outDir> — optional; defaults to _Processed\<host>\Services-Analyzer next to the app. A host named in a passed outDir wins over the path guess.
  • /from: /to: — case window (UTC, inclusive): prefills the date filter and is recorded in runinfo.json; never affects scoring.
  • Target hostname is required before processing and is cross-checked against the hive's ComputerName and the logs' Computer after a run — an amber chip on a mismatch, never a block.
  • Toolkit IOC list — an IOC.txt next to the app (one term per line, # comments) is merged into the IOC box at launch.

In the Artifact Finder every host with a config\SYSTEM hive gets a Services row beside Registry hives. [Process] launches this app on the host folder with the output folder and case window filled in (bulk mode adds /auto); after the run the row shows Processed and [Open] reloads the run. The Finder's processed inventory shows each run's triage summary (flagged of total, max score, top hits).

11  Limits & judgment calls

  • LastWrite is not install time. Anything that changes a value under the key updates it; servicing rewrites hundreds of keys at once (BULK). Use the install events for "when".
  • Display names stored as resource strings (@%SystemRoot%\…,-2) can't be resolved offline — those services join on key name, parentheses or image path instead.
  • 4697 needs auditing; without it installers appear as SIDs (named when any 4697 for that SID exists).
  • LOG-ONLY ≠ malicious — vendor updaters create and delete services too; read it with the image and installer.
  • Binaries are not hashed (they are rarely collected) — pivot to AmcacheParser-Wrapper or MFTECmd-Wrapper for SHA1 and file timestamps; for logon sessions and lateral movement use Login Activity Triage.
  • With no hive loaded, a 7045 and its 4697 that share an image with another install in the same two seconds — and whose names don't tie — are shown as two log-only records rather than risk joining the wrong pair.
  • Events-only folders holding several hosts' logs: the first System log is used and Security is filled only when it provably belongs to the same host — set the paths yourself for anything else.
  • Not covered: live-machine mode (config hives are locked), SOFTWARE-hive svchost group checks, the 7036 start / stop stream, unquoted-path hardening findings.

12  Troubleshooting

SymptomCause / fix
"RECmd Plugins folder incomplete"Plugins\RegistryPlugin.Services.dll is missing beside RECmd.exe — re-download RECmd with the button (the whole folder).
Status ends with "(dirty hive - processed without log replay)"The hive was dirty and its .LOG1/.LOG2 weren't beside it; the data is from the hive as collected. Collect the logs with the hive next time.
"Security.evtx: no 4697 events (auditing off?)"Security System Extension auditing wasn't enabled — 7045 still carries the installs.
Hive-only run when you expected logsEvtxECmd wasn't found — the status says so; use Update / download EvtxECmd.
"Access denied" / no CSV for a live C:\Windows\System32\config\SYSTEMLive hives are exclusively locked — collect first (Velociraptor / KAPE), then process the copy.
A very long evidence path shows a "Note: … over MAX_PATH" log lineExpected: mshta can't check paths over 260 characters, so it lets the engine read them (the engines handle long paths).
Running from a network share, accented names look wrongZone policy blocks the UTF-8 reader there; the app falls back to ANSI file IO. Copy the toolkit to a local folder for full fidelity.
Amber chip next to the hostnameThe hive's ComputerName (or the logs' Computer) differs from the Target hostname — check you picked the right host before filing the output.
